thread:
incident-bot: [PAGER] GPU driver Xid spike detected in inference-prod-us-west-2 - severity: page. 12 driver resets observed across 5 nodes in the last 10m. Affected pods: model-inference-*, redis-cache-*. Error sample: `Xid 79` and kernel oops observed. Auto-escalation to oncall.

maya (oncall): acked. I'm on it, pinging @dan and @sre-sarah. Can we get a quick impact summary? Which tenants are showing errors? :eyes:

dan (eng-runtime): seeing repeated `Xid 79` from nvidia-modeset driver. Logs: ```kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=27123, GPU has fallen off the bus``` Containers restarted due to liveness probes failing, ~8 pods restarted across 3 nodes. Two customer-facing flows (tenant: fastchat-inc, tenant: docstream) reported increased latency and 5% error rate on generation endpoints.

sre-sarah: oncall checklist: cordon affected nodes, start draining non-critical pods, escalate infra for node-level diagnostics. Also verify autoscaler didn't push faulty nodes.

jess (eng-runtime): we saw memory pressure before resets on node gpu-usw2-41 and gpu-usw2-43. KV-cache growth + long sequences increased GPU memory usage. Noticed a recent driver bump yesterday (nvidia-driver 535.101 -> 540.41) on those hosts. Could be driver regression with ECC handling.

liam (infra): noted. Confirming driver rollout window aligns. I'm preparing to pin workloads off the two most noisy hosts. Plan: cordon + drain gpu-usw2-41 and gpu-usw2-43; failover to dedicated warm pool. Will also collect `dmesg` and `nvidia-smi -q` outputs first.

maya (oncall): execute cordon/drain now if low risk. Keep me posted and open a customer bridge. @oliver can you prepare outbound to affected customers with ETA 30m for mitigation?

oliver (customer-success): on it. Drafting message: "We're investigating increased errors on generation endpoints in US-West. We're actively mitigating and expect partial restoration within 30-45 minutes. We'll follow up with root cause and mitigations." Will send once we have confirm of nodes being drained.

jess (eng-runtime): sequencing: 1) cordon+drain two noisy nodes 2) add capacity in warm pool (scale up dedicated) 3) if resets persist, roll back driver to 535.101 on drained nodes and run soak. I'm cautious about driver rollback timing.

liam (infra): running commands now: ```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-usw2-41
kubectl drain gpu-usw2-41 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --grace-period=60
``` Output: ```node/gpu-usw2-41 cordoned
pod/model-inference-abc evicted
pod/redis-cache-02 evicted
drain completed (some pods failed graceful termination and were force deleted)```

incident-bot: Note: autoscaler triggered 2 additional nodes in warm pool (dedicated-warm-6, dedicated-warm-7) to help capacity.

dan (eng-runtime): After drain, telemetry shows error rate drop to ~2.1% on affected endpoints; latency back to baseline for most requests. Still seeing one node (gpu-usw2-43) with intermittent Xid spikes. Collecting `nvidia-bug-report.sh` outputs and GPU core dumps.

sre-sarah: If Xid continues after drain, recommend kernel module reload and driver soft-restart before full reimage. Commands to try on the node (careful, will disrupt running pods if any): ```bash
sudo systemctl stop kubelet
sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm nvidia_modeset nvidia
sudo modprobe nvidia nvidia_modeset nvidia_uvm
sudo systemctl start kubelet
``` Note: this often clears transient hangs but not ECC parity faults.

jess (eng-runtime): ran soft-restart sequence on gpu-usw2-43 now. `nvidia-smi` shows all GPUs present. Dmesg still has occasional Xid 79 but frequency decreased. We'll keep node cordoned and run longer soak tests.

liam (infra): initiating driver rollback on drained nodes to 535.101: ```ansible-playbook -i production rollback-nvidia-driver.yml -e driver_version=535.101 -l gpu-usw2-41,gpu-usw2-43``` Playbook output: `changed=4 failed=0` -- drivers replaced and modules rebuilt. Rebooting hosts to complete.

incident-bot: Automated customer-impact tracker: impacted-tenants=["fastchat-inc","docstream"], error_rate_peak=5.2%, restored_pct=78%, action=drain+rollback.

maya (oncall): good progress. @oliver please update customers with mitigation steps started and expected time to full recovery 60m. Also open bridge for execs if needed.

oliver (customer-success): updated customers at 14:12 UTC. Called primary contact for fastchat-inc; they asked for an interim workaround (route queries to eu-west region). Provided steps and flags.

dan (eng-runtime): post-rollback and reboot telemetry: stable. No driver resets observed for 20m on rolled-back nodes. Error rate back to ~0.5% overall. We'll uncordon after soak.

sre-sarah: uncordon plan: run canary traffic to nodes for 15m, check metrics (Xid count, GPU mem pressure, liveness). If stable, gradually reassign production workloads.

liam (infra): uncordoning gpu-usw2-41 now: `kubectl uncordon gpu-usw2-41` -> `node/gpu-usw2-41 uncordoned`. Starting canary scheduler.

jess (eng-runtime): canary looks clean after 22m. No new Xid events. Rolling back autoscaler scaling to baseline.

maya (oncall): handing off to @dan and @sre-sarah for root-cause and postmortem. Event summary: cause suspected driver regression in 540.41 interacting with long-sequence KV cache memory patterns causing GPU memory churn leading to Xid 79 driver resets. Mitigation: cordon+drain, driver rollback to 535.101, reboot, soak, and gradual reintegration. Impact: partial degradation for two tenants (~30-45m window) with peak error rate 5.2%.

dan (eng-runtime): assigning postmortem owner: dan. Next actions: gather nv-bug-report, `dmesg` logs, compare driver state across fleet, evaluate bump gating for drivers, add rollout safety (small canary windows + mem/stress tests with long-seq kv-cache reproducer).

sre-sarah: tagging incident with severity P2 for now. Will open incident ticket INC-2026-149. Docs: add mitigation runbook for driver Xid spikes with step-by-step commands and rollback playbook.

maya (oncall): closing paging thread; if new spikes appear reopen. Thanks team. :clap:
